normalized_outcome: Mission Control uses one remotely hosted active submission authority on the owner-authorized 16 GB primary VPS and one fail-closed 8 GB standby VPS. Every ChatGPT send is admitted and durably recorded by one central scheduler enforcing the global minimum interval; only explicitly MC-only conversations and automation-owned browser targets are eligible; controlled failover cannot create split brain; the owner computer's browser windows, tabs and clipboard are outside the routine execution path. Portable controls remain reusable while this owner's deployment facts are explicitly isolated and labelled non-universal.

required_outcomes.observable: Retained Hostinger relay records yield exact observed ChatGPT click times and intervals, plus a truthful determination of whether the pre-change implementation had a central cross-host queue and per-send admission gate.

All relay send paths use one scheduler that serializes the queue, issues a single-use admission before browser mutation, persists the admission and actual send boundary, and enforces the configured global minimum interval.

The supervisor registry requires an explicit Mission Control-only ownership classification and registration provenance; personal, ambiguous, legacy-unclassified, wrong-owner and wrong-target conversations fail closed before send.

The exact reviewed relay/controller candidate is installed on the 16 GB owner-authorized primary VPS with a private independent browser profile and healthy no-send checks; the 8 GB owner-authorized VPS remains a healthy, disabled standby using the same candidate.

Failover is active/passive and fail closed: only one deployment lease/epoch can admit sends, standby cannot submit, takeover requires proven primary quiescence, pacing-state transfer, and a full safety interval after the later of the last possible boundary and quiescence proof; ambiguous partition/split-brain state blocks both sides.

Routine Mission Control work uses only the remote execution host's dedicated automation-owned browser/profile and direct browser-protocol text input; no owner-local browser window/tab and no owner/user clipboard read or write is used.

The previously merged exact browser-window/target ownership isolation, loopback browser control, native sandbox, one bounded rate-limit acknowledgement/retry, and stronger global minimum interval remain mechanically enforced and regression-tested.

Reusable multi-host architecture is documented as portable guidance; every owner-specific provider label, hostname, service ID, machine path and topology fact is isolated under explicit NON_UNIVERSAL / EXAMPLE_OWNER_DEPLOYMENT labelling; secrets, credentials and private chat locators are absent from Git.

Mission Control execution workers themselves, not only the browser relay/controller, run on the owner-authorized remote primary with the secondary as failover; the owner's local Codex/Work host is not the routine worker execution surface.

one in-process Promise chain represented as a cross-host central scheduler
a route being admitted upstream without a fresh single-use browser-send permit
a matching chat URL without Mission Control-only conversation ownership provenance
automation-owned browser target proof without separate conversation ownership proof
copying the authenticated Hostinger browser profile or cookies to Netcup
installing code on Netcup without a healthy independent no-send browser/runtime check
moving only the browser relay/controller while leaving routine Mission Control execution workers on the owner's local Codex/Work host
calling Hostinger a failover while it can submit concurrently with Netcup
documentation or unit tests represented as live host health
using Joel's local browser or clipboard because the remote browser is unavailable
placing private hostnames, IPs, credentials, service identifiers, chat locators or machine paths in reusable public templates
a green pull request without installing the exact reviewed candidate on both authorized hosts
deploying or mutating Railway production or any third host
production_boundary: Only the two owner-authorized Mission Control infrastructure VPS hosts are in deployment scope; Railway production and every other host remain unauthorized.
